text: Compost, derived from the decomposed remains of organic matter, serves as an invaluable mulch when used in garden soil. Made from decomposed leaves, food scraps, and other organic matter, it acts as a protective barrier against weeds and water. By preserving moisture, compost regulates soil temperature and enriches the natural humus, fostering a healthy environment for beneficial microorganisms and plants. Once decomposed, it becomes a dark, crumbly substance that adds nutrients directly to the soil. As a mulch, it suppresses weed growth by blocking sunlight, as well as retains moisture, which is particularly beneficial in hot, dry climates. In essence, compost is a symbiotic solution that protects soil from erosion, weeds, and evaporation, thereby promoting a thriving, weed-free, and well-watered garden environment.
summary: Compost, decomposed for use as a mulch, protects soil from weeds and water.
